## ACCEPTED on substance — PR #8105. ⛔ Ready-flip held: CI started 15:37Z and has not converged.

Engine-core seat #6019, `session_014C8pAprWdmtecFsEprZax4`. Read from the diff, ⛔ not from the report.

### The predicate equivalence, checked here rather than taken on trust

The refusal moved out of the mutation walk, so the whole fix rests on the new pass deciding **exactly** what the inline check decided. Reading both:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| ownership test | per-contrib `contrib.ownership === 'own'` while iterating this package's contributions | `contributors.some(c => c.packageId === packageId && c.ownership === 'own')` |
| extender set | `contributors.filter(c => c.packageId !== packageId && c.ownership === 'extend')` | **identical expression** |
| iteration | `this.objectContributors.entries()` | **same map, same order** |
| `force` | `!force` guarding the inline check | `if (!force)` wrapping the whole pass |

The ownership rewrite is the only shape change, and it is equivalent: "does this package own this object" is the same question whether you ask it per-contribution or with `.some()` over the same list. ⭐ And the equivalence is not left as my reading — the **message-identity test passes against the pre-fix `registry.ts`**, which is a stronger proof than any argument I could make from the diff. That test was written to be green on both sides *on purpose*; a test that only passes after the fix could not have shown this.

### The test set is the right shape

**3 red on revert / 3 green under both**, with the other **93 unmoved** — so nothing in the existing suite depended on the old ordering, which is the fact that makes this safe to land as a "consistency fix, not new policy".

⭐ The one I asked for is there and is doing exactly its job: `refuses before removing anything — a free sibling object survives`, with `free` registered **first** so the Map walk reaches it before it can refuse. Its comment says why it is the discriminating case, and the PR says the rest out loud — *"a single-object fixture passes under the namespace-only fix, this one does not."* That is the difference between the fix I dispatched and the fix that was needed, pinned in a test rather than asserted in a PR body.

The `force: true` pin matters more than it looks: the refusal pass is now skipped wholesale under `force`, so "force removes exactly what it removed before" is a real risk surface, and it is pinned with three assertions including the extender's own contribution surviving.

### The scope call, confirmed against the ruling's refusals

The second limb is fixed by **ordering inside the verb** — refusal pass, then mutation pass — with a comment that names the alternative and why it was not taken (*"a second copy of the predicate here is the two-places-that-must-agree shape this ordering fix was chosen over"*). ⛔ Not option 2 (no `canUninstall` probe), ⛔ not option 3 (no journal, no rollback). Both refused by name in triage; neither is in the diff.

And `unregisterObjectsByPackage` now **documents the guarantee** — a throw is a no-op — which is what makes it safe for `MetadataFacade.unregisterPackage` and `ObjectQL.unregisterObject` to call it ahead of their own mutations. Those two callers were exposed to the same partial walk and are fixed by the same change without being touched.

### The #7951 question was answered by measurement, and the answer is *no*

I asked whether the orphan-report surface was a literal one-line rider here. Measured answer: **it is not** — `uninstallPackage` returns `boolean`, so surfacing `{ removed, orphanedOverlays }` changes its return contract and every caller's read of it. That is a product decision and it stays with #7951.

⭐ **And nothing was filed for it**, deliberately, because #7951 already covers it. That is the right call: a duplicate card costs more than the observation is worth, and the guidance to file out-of-scope findings is not a quota. ⛔ Do not read the empty `out_of_scope_findings` as a thin run.

| check | reading |
|---|---|
| **path face** (`get_files`) | `.changeset/…`, `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`, `registry.test.ts` — ⛔ no `docs/adr/**`, no skills root. Clean |
| PR first line | `Fixes #7970` — correct; the merge should close the card |
| changeset | present, `@objectstack/objectql` **patch**, and it states the behaviour change in both limbs plus what is *unchanged* (message, `force`, successful path). Correct severity for a latent fix |
| grade | left **latent** — ⛔ not inflated to an incident. No in-tree caller reaches the refusal path |
| ratchets | `check:query-options-erasure` and `check:type-check-debt --re-measure` both run on a **full built closure** (71/71), no baseline raised, `--lower` not run, no ledger file in the diff |

### Why it is not flipped yet

At ~15:5xZ: 12 concluded, **0 failure**; `ESLint`, `TypeScript Type Check`, all three `Test Core` shards, all three `Dogfood` shards, `Temporal Conformance` and `Build Core` still `in_progress`. ⛔ Not flipping on an absence of visible failures — and on this card less than any other, since it is the only behaviour change of the shift. Next patrol reads the job conclusions; all-green ⇒ ready + enqueue SQUASH.

⚠️ One note for whoever meets this seam next, worth more than the fix: **it had three addresses in one day** — `:2586-2608` (triage), `:2636-2667` (branch point), `:2725` (post-merge), in a 3,000-line file that took two unrelated merges in that window. The PR body records it. Locate by symbol.
